## 固定收益開場論點

6月24日，美國公債全線上漲。油價進一步重挫，降低未來能源對通膨的推升力道；疲弱的房市指標則增添證據，顯示高昂借款成本正在抑制對利率敏感的經濟部門。漲勢主要集中於前端以外：5年期殖利率下降9.2個基點至4.177%，10年期下降10.5個基點至4.393%，30年期下降10.6個基點至4.841%；2年期則下降5.1個基點至4.148%。

殖利率曲線因而呈現牛市趨平，2年與10年期利差收窄5.4個基點至24.5個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄5.5個基點至69.3個基點。前一交易日的行情主要由通膨補償下降帶動，週三名目公債的漲勢則同時獲得10年期殖利率兩項組成因素支持：10年期實質殖利率下降7.8個基點至2.201%，損益兩平通膨率下降2.7個基點至2.192%。投資人一方面下修通膨補償所含的能源風險，另一方面在房市數據轉弱、原油下跌使債券需求擴大之際，接受較低的實質報酬。

隨著通過荷莫茲海峽的油輪增加，實體供給重返一度受美伊衝突干擾的市場，布蘭特原油收跌4.33%至$73.74，WTI下跌3.92%至$70.34。即使美國商用原油庫存減少610萬桶，油價仍然下跌。汽油與餾分油庫存增加、煉油產能利用率達96.1%，加上海灣地區出口復甦的跡象，使原油庫存降幅的重要性不及成品油供應改善與航運信心回升。

這波漲勢並不代表市場否定聯準會的緊縮傾向。市場先前一度充分反映截至2027年中升息2次，目前仍定價約40個基點的額外緊縮；美元指數上漲0.20%至101.61。黃金期貨下跌3.38%至每盎司$3,990.30，在美國利率預期上升、美元走強及地緣政治避險需求減弱之下延續跌勢。美債與美元同步上漲，反映市場正在重新評估聯準會多快會需要採取行動，而非認為基礎通膨已回到目標。

財政部標售$700億5年期公債，最高得標殖利率4.200%、投標倍數2.35倍；大規模供給順利消化，曲線中段漲勢得以延續。信用市場的表現更具選擇性：政府債殖利率下降帶動投資級債價格上揚，高收益債基金幾乎持平；Hertz提出非比尋常、偏防禦性的可轉換債融資方案，印度Shapoorji Pallonji Group則向債權人爭取更多時間。當日市場一方面出現廣泛的利率債漲勢，另一方面也再次顯示，基準殖利率下降無法消除個別發行人的再融資風險。

## 油價壓力緩解擴大美債漲勢

能源前景最重要的變化來自實體運輸，而非外交進展。船隻開啟衛星訊號通過荷莫茲海峽，顯示船東對安全通行的信心提高。國際海事組織表示，船舶可使用伊朗水域，或採行由阿曼與美國協調的航線；該組織也已取得安全保證，涵蓋數百艘尋求駛離波斯灣的船隻。

肥料運輸同樣改善，至少16艘載運作物養分的船舶駛出海峽，運量逐步接近戰前水準。國際能源總署指出，阿拉伯聯合大公國6月上旬的石油出口已恢復至戰前速度的近85%；卡達則預期，未受損設施的液化天然氣產量可在數週內恢復正常。這些進展意味著潛在供給回升不再只限於伊朗原油，也降低運輸中斷延續先前能源衝擊的可能性。

政治協議仍不完整。華府與德黑蘭對核查及獲釋伊朗資金的控制權各有說法，荷莫茲海峽的長期管理也尚未達成安排。伊朗尋求正式角色，並提出可能帶來費用收入的保險規定；以色列與伊朗支持團體若持續交戰，仍可能使局勢再度升高。不過，隨著可見貨運量增加、歐洲與亞洲的原油供應報價增加，市場認為這些風險的急迫性已經下降。

這項轉變一度將WTI推至$70以下，終場收在$70.34；布蘭特原油則收於$74以下。當日跌幅使WTI近1個月累計下跌27.18%，布蘭特原油下跌28.78%。現貨與期貨價格下滑，降低能源對整體通膨的預期貢獻；但先前漲價已經透過生產、運輸與服務傳導，央行官員與交易員仍保持警覺。

美國石油報告顯示，不能只看原油庫存來判斷通膨影響。商用原油庫存減少610萬桶至4.121億桶，比5年同期平均低約7%。汽油庫存增加210萬桶至2.163億桶，仍比5年平均低約5%；餾分油庫存增加310萬桶至1.061億桶，比平均低約10%。煉油廠產能利用率達96.1%。

過去4週的石油產品日均供應量為2,050萬桶，比一年前增加2.1%；同期間汽油需求則比去年同期低3.0%。這組數據呈現的市場狀況是：即使原油庫存下降，煉油廠仍以高負荷運轉，成品油庫存也正在回補。儘管絕對庫存偏低、地緣政治條件尚未解決，這樣的組合仍支持眼前短缺風險正在減輕的判斷。

房市則提供了與能源行情相呼應的美國內需訊號。5月新屋銷售不如預期，建築許可也弱於預估，再次顯示具限制性的房貸利率正在壓抑住宅需求與營建活動。這些數據本身不足以證明經濟全面收縮，卻使市場更難再將整體經濟視為對高實質利率一概具有韌性。這點對5年至30年期券種尤其重要，因為市場正同時衡量持續的通膨，以及限制性融資條件逐步累積的影響。

投資人消化上述訊號之際，美債交易活動顯著增加。FINRA記錄的面額交易量達$1.460兆，比6月23日增加29.0%；名目附息債交易量增加29.9%至$1.111兆。剩餘期限超過3年、至5年的券種交易量大增61.4%至$3,350億，超過7年、至10年的券種交易量增加41.9%至$1,962億。這些數字衡量的是雙向交易而非淨買進，但交易最集中的區段，正是當日領漲並承接主要附息債標售的券種。

TIPS交易量增幅較小，上升6.6%至$307億。這項差異與殖利率變動的組成一致：通膨補償繼續下降，但更大幅度的調整來自實質殖利率。即使週三下跌，10年期實質殖利率仍比1個月前高5.5個基點；10年期損益兩平通膨率則低22.1個基點。因此，當日行情收回聯準會會議後實質折現率升幅的一部分，卻未恢復先前因油價重挫而消失的通膨溢價。

美元與貴金屬呈現這輪政策重新定價的另一面。美元指數近1週上漲1.52%，近1個月上漲2.31%。金價自去年11月以來首次跌破每盎司$4,000，近1個月累計下跌11.74%。白銀跌幅更大，鉑金與鈀金也同步走弱。

聯準會主席Kevin Warsh強調恢復物價穩定，提高了可提供收益的美元資產的相對吸引力，但他並未主張升息是唯一可採取的措施。財政部長Scott Bessent表示，隨著伊朗衝突降溫，他預期通膨會回落，並相信Warsh會獨立權衡通膨與成長。這項預期仍有前提：週四數據公布前的預測顯示，5月整體PCE通膨年增率可能為4.1%，核心通膨為3.4%，均遠高於聯準會目標。

標普500指數下跌0.10%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.43%，道瓊指數則上漲0.4%。指數波動看似有限，但掩蓋了美光公布業績前科技股持續疲弱，以及多數標普500成分股上漲的分化。油價下降支撐整體股市，限制性利率前景則繼續壓抑對遠期企業獲利較敏感的股票估值。VIX下降4.41%至18.63，說明即使美債上漲，當日也不是全面避險行情。

## 5年期供給順利消化，美債槓桿曝險升高

財政部新發行的5年期公債最高得標殖利率為4.200%，票息4⅛%。投資人提出$1,644.27億競爭性投標，得標金額為$698.55億，投標倍數2.35倍。間接投標人獲配$430.28億，直接投標人獲配$178.20億，一級交易商承接$90.06億。債券於6月30日交割，2031年6月30日到期。

由於未提供發行前交易殖利率，無法判定本次標售出現尾差或穿越發行前水準。更有用的訊號是，大規模中期債供給在市場上漲期間順利消化，並未迫使行情反轉。直接與間接投標人合計取得競爭性發行的大部分，一級交易商承接金額則低於$100億。前一天2年期公債標售已顯示投資人願意吸收政策敏感及中期利率風險，本次結果延續了這項趨勢。

當日浮動利率債的投標倍數更高。財政部增額發行$280億、剩餘期限1年10個月的浮動利率債，最高得標折價利差為0.079%，利差0.103%，指標利率決定值3.695%，投標倍數2.99倍。在$279.81億競爭性得標金額中，間接投標人承接$186.50億，一級交易商承接$93.31億，直接投標人未獲配。該券於6月26日交割，2028年4月30日到期。

短票方面，$690億、119天期國庫券的最高得標折價率為3.770%，投資收益率3.871%，投標倍數2.55倍；按最高得標利率投標者獲配11.15%。競爭性得標中，間接投標人承接$374.14億，一級交易商承接$284.95億，直接投標人承接$25.73億。該券於6月30日交割，10月27日到期。國庫券與浮動利率債的結果均未顯示市場在吸收現金管理型供給時有明顯困難，但因缺乏發行前交易參考，無法判斷其定價相對標售前市場的表現。

聯準會最新發布的研究，將上述初級市場結果置於美債中介結構的長期變化下觀察。首席經濟學家Phillip Monin估計，截至9月，現券期貨基差交易占避險基金美債多頭部位$8,300億，約為2020年初高峰的兩倍，也占其多頭曝險總額的35%。這項策略以放空美債期貨搭配透過附買回融資持有可交割現券，利用高度槓桿賺取細微價差。

2023年9月至2025年9月間，避險基金的美債總曝險增加一倍至$4兆，其中多頭部位$2.4兆、空頭部位$1.6兆。基差與交換利差套利占多頭部位近半，其餘分布於殖利率曲線策略、未設擔保的現券持有及單純多頭用途。自2023年初以來，總曝險、附買回借款及每月美債成交量都已增加逾一倍。

部位集中度也在上升。規模最大的50檔基金占避險基金美債總曝險90%，高於先前的84%。Monin指出，如果多項策略同時承壓，或嚴重衝擊波及最大型參與者，相關規模、槓桿與集中度可能造成系統性壓力。基差交易在正常環境下有助於價格發現與流動性，但2020年3月類似部位迅速平倉，曾加劇美債市場動盪。

這項研究描述的是市場結構，而非週三投資人的交易方向；然而，在現券交易活絡、初級供給龐大時，其意義仍不容忽視。槓桿套利可串連標售債券、期貨與附買回市場，在正常交易環境下擴大市場承接能力；但如果保證金上升、附買回條件收緊，或相對價值關係朝不利於擁擠部位的方向變動，同樣的結構也會迅速傳遞融資或波動衝擊。

## 信用市場區分利率利多與再融資風險

美債殖利率下降帶動投資級債券基金LQD上漲0.46%；高收益債價格則近乎持平，HYG下跌0.03%，JNK下跌0.06%。新興市場債券基金EMB上漲0.32%。這項表現顯示，存續期部位受惠於利率債上漲，但投資人並未不加區分地追捧較低品質的企業信用風險。

紐約聯準銀行6月企業債市場壓力指數提供了更廣泛的市場運作衡量。整體市場狀況在當月改善，月底略高於該指數歷史分布的第20百分位。投資級市場運作約在歷史第50百分位，高收益債壓力則維持在歷史低檔。這項研究指標綜合初級市場發行與定價、次級市場流動性及交易指標，不等同於信用利差的絕對水準或單日方向。

整體市場運作有序，個別發行人卻同時面臨尖銳壓力。Hertz宣布發行$3億以債付息（PIK）可轉換債，並同步發行$1億新股，供可轉債投資人借入後放空。Hertz股權集中，股票又已遭大量放空，可供借券的股票稀少，這項結構正是為處理該限制而設計。

以債付息讓公司不必支付傳統現金票息，可轉換結構的成本也應低於直接發行高收益債。Hertz計畫以所得資金償還既有債務；部分循環信用額度本月到期，因而騰出增加第一順位留置權借款的空間。融資利益伴隨股權稀釋：按指示價格計算，發行股數將超過2,500萬股，相當於流通股數約21%。

公司先前警告，二手車價格意外疲弱將提高折舊費用，之後提出此次籌資。Hertz預估第2季調整後企業稅息折舊及攤銷前盈餘不會超過$8,000萬，低於分析師預期。公司股價重挫41%，創2021年掛牌以來最大跌幅。美債殖利率下降雖降低融資成本中的基準利率部分，擬議條款仍反映公司本身保存現金與避險方面的限制。

Shapoorji Pallonji Group面臨更直接的到期壓力。這家印度企業集團向債券持有人提出30個基點費用，希望取得同意，再次延長Goswami Infratech發行的零息債。集團尋求將1,430億盧比、約$15億的還款日延後至6月30日到期日至少1個月之後。

Goswami債券自2023年發行以來，未償本金已降至834.2億盧比，但殖利率由發行時的18.75%升至21.75%。集團也希望把融資單位Porteast Investment一項債務條款的期限，由7月15日延至9月30日。Porteast先前把一筆$34億貸款的貸款成數上限由34%暫時提高至40%；隨著Tata Consultancy Services股價在近6年低點附近交易，擔保該筆債務的抵押品價值已經下降。

多數貸款人已同意擬議變更，但Ares Management仍是持續協商者之一。相關債務以集團持有的Tata Sons 18.4%股權作為擔保。因此，這項要求仍處於徵求同意階段，並非已完成的再融資；若繼續延宕，Goswami與Porteast債務最終如何償還仍將充滿不確定性。

私人信用曝險則帶來另一種警訊。避險基金經理人Lee Robinson正使用信用違約交換放空Lincoln National、MetLife及Berkshire Hathaway等保險公司，理由是市場尚未充分反映私人債務可能出現的減記。美國保險公司CDS的淨名目部位由2025年底不到$49億，增至5月22日的$55億；交易量與避險成本也同步上升。

這項論點並不是大型保險公司正面臨立即性的生存威脅。MetLife表示，其私人債務投資組合約95%屬投資級，配置充分分散，設計上可穿越市場週期。不過，Moody’s分析顯示，截至2025年底，美國壽險公司$4兆固定收益資產中，有五分之一為非流動資產，且大多是私人信用，高於一年前的18%。Moody’s也發現中型企業直接貸款開始出現壓力，包括信用品質轉弱與借款人壓力升高。

這與紐約聯準銀行壓力指數形成重要對照。公開企業債市場仍運作順暢，高收益債壓力也維持歷史低檔；但投資人正付出更高成本，針對部分保險公司與透明度較低私人資產相關的風險進行避險。因此，整體信用環境偏緊而有序，仍可能與防範局部損失或流動性事件的避險需求累積並存。

追求額外收益也正在改變企業財務主管的投資組合。Clearwater Analytics針對逾400家公司、約$1兆資產所做的研究發現，企業財務主管目前持有Rule 144A債券的中位數占比為2%，數年前則幾乎為零。這類證券通常在合格機構投資人之間交易，流動性可能低於公開註冊債券。

這些私募債通常在2年或更久後到期，相較存續期間相近的同類高評級債券，平均可提供約52個基點的殖利率溢酬。額外收益正吸引現金管理人降低傳統上集中配置國庫券與商業本票的程度。Clearwater認為市場對系統性風險的憂慮遭到誇大，但也承認個別標的存在弱點；這項區分與公開市場壓力指標仍有序、個別借款人融資卻更困難的情況一致。

阿根廷則提供一個融資條件改善、但未循傳統國際發債途徑的主權案例。政府已籌得7月9日支付$42億債券款項所需的美元，平均硬通貨融資成本約6.7%，比估計的國際發債成本低約200個基點。財政部美元存款已達約$36億，足以支付約85%的款項，其餘預計來自境內美元融資、央行購匯及多邊機構支持的融資。

評等調升與國家風險降至約430個基點，較數月前至少低100個基點，均有利於這項策略。即使條件改善，阿根廷紐約法債券曲線的殖利率仍在9%左右，國際借款成本依舊偏高。政府已授權最多$50億、由世界銀行及美洲開發銀行等機構支持的融資；經濟部長Luis Caputo估計成本接近6%。

避開華爾街降低了因應眼前到期款項的成本，卻未解決2027年的再融資規畫。分析師表示，如果外部條件持續有利，阿根廷最終可能發行$50億至$80億債券。目前的成果範圍較窄：7月款項已大致完成融資，且不必接受全球債券投資人要求的溢價。

## 能源轉便宜，各國央行仍保留升息選項

油價下跌並未帶來一致的全球政策反應。日本央行將政策利率升至1%、創1995年以來最高後，其《意見摘要》進一步支持後續升息。一名委員表示，基礎通膨正接近2%，金融環境仍然寬鬆；隨著經濟與物價演變，繼續升息是適當做法。

另一項意見估計中性利率約為2%，並建議考慮每隔數月升息；另有委員主張應儘快使利率更接近中性。日本央行本身估計的中性利率區間為1.1%至2.5%，即使6月升息，目前利率仍接近區間下緣。

日本央行總裁植田和男出院後，由副總裁冰見野良三代為宣讀談話。植田表示，通膨可能超過2%目標，並重申央行會依經濟活動、物價及金融狀況調整寬鬆程度；升息時點與速度也部分取決於伊朗衝突。企業服務價格已連續第3個月年增3.3%，支持通膨壓力並非僅來自進口商品的疑慮。

日圓維持在每美元161.60附近，接近1986年以來最低水準。對依賴資源進口的經濟體而言，日圓疲弱會提高輸入性通膨，也使當局持續警戒匯率過度波動。政治限制仍在：審議委員朝田照一反對6月升息，另有一名政府任命的新委員將於月底加入政策委員會。不過，目前的溝通仍顯示，多數委員把1%視為寬鬆水準，而非升息終點。

印度的市場方向相反。印度儲備銀行總裁Sanjay Malhotra表示，現在討論升息仍嫌過早；如果緊縮的可能性足夠高，決策官員在6月會議便會把立場由中性調整為限制性。印度儲備銀行最終維持政策利率5.25%不變，並保留依數據決策的立場。

印度10年期公債殖利率下降5個基點至6.82%，創3個月低點；5年期隔夜指數交換利率下跌10個基點至6.17%。花旗放棄本財政年度升息的預測；HDFC Bank也不再預期2027財政年度結束前升息，除非天候引發的通膨成為持續性問題。

但限制條件仍然重要。印度約90%的石油仰賴進口，原油回落可直接降低其通膨曝險；然而，截至6月22日，累計季風降雨量比正常水準低43%，若缺雨持續，可能威脅農業生產與農村需求。Malhotra表示，糧食緩衝庫存足以減輕產量下降的影響，但也強調停火協議仍然脆弱，石油供給尚未完全正常化。

中國的寬鬆前景也變得較不確定。受訪的33名經濟學家中，略多於一半預期中國人民銀行在2026年底前維持政策利率不變，其餘則預期年底前小幅降息。中國人民銀行貨幣政策委員會委員黃益平表示，仍可能降息，但並無保證；他並主張針對科技與民生提供更精準的支持。

中國第2季經濟已經放緩。5月零售銷售出現疫情管制解封以來首次萎縮，固定資產投資也比預期疲弱。全球AI投資熱潮支撐進出口，但油價仍高於一年前。5月消費者通膨停滯，工廠端價格卻以近4年最快速度上升。銀行利差狹窄、借款需求疲弱及房地產低迷，均削弱全面降息的效果，7月底政治局會議因此成為下一個主要政策觀察窗口。

歐洲央行持續釋出訊號，顯示油價轉低並未終結升息討論。執行委員Isabel Schnabel表示，要讓中期通膨回到2%，可能仍需進一步升息。升息幅度與時點取決於衝突、經濟及通膨情勢，但她警告，停火不代表可以放鬆警戒。

Schnabel強調，即使現貨市場回落，遠期能源價格仍處高檔。她表示，5月通膨顯示最初的能源衝擊已有部分擴散，但尚無證據顯示出現第二輪效應。她認為目前利率並不具限制性，歐元區經濟的韌性也比預期強。多數投資人與經濟學家預期至少再升息25個基點一次，將存款利率推升至2.5%。

克羅埃西亞央行總裁Ante Zigman成為歐洲央行管理委員會中偏重通膨一方的新聲音。他就任後首次公開發言時表示，物價穩定是歐洲央行的首要任務，荷莫茲海峽恢復通行將有助於通膨降溫。他支持及早採取行動，反映歐洲央行面臨的矛盾：油價下降改善未來整體通膨路徑，但官員仍擔心先前衝擊已進入更廣泛的價格形成過程。

德國ifo商業景氣指數則稍微緩解成長疑慮。6月整體指數由5月的85.0升至85.6，企業對當前情勢的評估改善，預期也略減悲觀。製造業預期增強，但當前狀況轉弱，新訂單再度下降；貿易與營建業信心改善，服務業者則回報當前業務好轉、預期大致不變。數據降低眼前下行疑慮，卻不足以證明經濟將強勁復甦。

墨西哥在政策決策前出現更明確的通膨意外。6月上半月消費者物價年增3.55%，低於調查中的所有預測；調查中位數為3.72%。核心通膨降至4.12%，大致符合4.13%的預期。內需疲弱有助於抑制物價，但服務通膨下降仍相當緩慢，食品與能源價格也持續波動。

市場預期墨西哥央行將維持隔夜利率6.50%不變。總裁Victoria Rodríguez曾表示，目前利率水準適合引導通膨朝3%目標回落；若需求持續疲弱且通膨預期保持穩定，也不排除再次調整。整體通膨低於預期強化鴿派理據，但核心通膨仍高於4%，支持央行在先前降息後維持暫停，評估改善能否持續。

儘管全球曾受能源衝擊，新加坡5月核心通膨仍維持1.4%，低於1.6%的預估中位數，與4月相同。這項結果支持新加坡金融管理局7月決策時維持匯率政策設定不變的預期；該局4月才收緊政策。智利方面，會議紀錄顯示，5名央行理事一致認為6月唯一合理選項是把政策利率維持在4.5%。美伊協議降低了緊縮政策的可能性，但官員希望先看到和平進程能夠延續，再改變政策方向。

澳洲則更堅定地聚焦國內通膨。澳洲儲備銀行副總裁Andrew Hauser表示，經濟可能正處於菲利普曲線較陡峭的區段，亦即超額需求會引發更大的通膨反應。這是央行今年前三次會議均升息的理由之一。澳洲央行上週在4.35%暫停升息，但仍保留再次調高利率的選項。

Hauser指出，菲利普曲線同樣的陡峭特性也意味著，只要及時緊縮，央行或能以較小的失業增幅壓低通膨。澳洲央行預期，通膨要到2028年中才會回到2%至3%目標區間的中點，失業率高峰則為4.7%。油價下降有助減輕供給衝擊，但央行仍擔心國內通膨過高，且中東衝突尚未完全解決。

## 後續市場意義

眼前首要考驗是6月25日美東時間08:30公布的美國數據，包括5月PCE通膨、個人所得與支出、耐久財訂單、第1季GDP第3次估值及首次申領失業救濟金人數。數據公布前所引用的預測顯示，5月整體PCE通膨年增率為4.1%，核心通膨為3.4%。即使油價已大幅下跌，這樣的物價增幅仍遠高於目標。

數據組成與整體通膨數字同樣重要。若基礎物價堅挺、支出具有韌性，將支持聯準會的緊縮傾向，也會考驗這波已使10年期實質殖利率下降近8個基點的美債漲勢。若需求或勞動數據轉弱，尤其核心物價壓力也同步緩和，則會強化房市透露的疲弱訊號，也增添聯準會暫緩行動的理由。這批數據將決定當日牛市趨平究竟反映市場更廣泛地重新評估限制性政策，還是主要只是能源風險下降所帶來的舒緩。

財政部將於美東時間11:30標售$700億4週期國庫券及$750億8週期國庫券，13:00再標售$440億新發行7年期公債，3批券均於6月30日交割。另有一項針對剩餘期限20年至30年名目附息債的買回，於13:40至14:00進行。在10年與30年期殖利率均下降逾10個基點後，7年期標售將檢驗週三順利吸收5年期公債的需求能否進一步延伸至曲線較長區段。

歐洲央行將於中歐夏令時間10:00發布《經濟公報》。市場會把其中對6月決策及工作人員預測的細節，與Schnabel主張進一步升息、Zigman強調物價穩定，以及德國ifo調查改善相互比較。關鍵在於，能源現貨價格下跌是否實質降低中期通膨壓力，還是先前漲價已廣泛傳導後，只讓短期路徑稍微轉弱。

墨西哥央行將於美東時間15:00公布決策，目前隔夜利率為6.50%。6月上半月通膨低於預期，讓決策官員有更多空間討論未來降息；但核心通膨仍達4.12%，服務價格壓力也持續存在，支持審慎行事。相較於單純維持利率不變，央行對疲弱內需與披索的指引將更具影響力。

6月26日日本時間08:30將公布6月東京CPI初值，這是日本央行把利率升至1%後，首項反映當月通膨的測試。若數據偏強，尤其基礎項目堅挺，將支持主張每隔數月升息的委員；若數據較弱，植田和男附帶條件的措辭，以及政治上對快速正常化的阻力，重要性將隨之上升。

密西根大學消費者調查終值與紐約聯準銀行多變量核心趨勢通膨指標，將於6月26日美東時間10:00公布。密西根大學初值顯示，消費者信心為48.9，1年期通膨預期4.6%，長期通膨預期3.4%。終值修正將顯示油價回落是否已開始改變家庭看法；紐約聯準銀行指標則會從另一角度檢驗，基礎通膨是否仍與聯準會較具限制性的政策立場一致。

overall_summary.headline: 油價重挫、房市疲弱，美債呈牛市趨平
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國公債全線上漲，由中期與長期券領漲。5年期殖利率下降9.2個基點至4.177%，10年期下降10.5個基點至4.393%，30年期下降10.6個基點至4.841%；2年期則下降5.1個基點至4.148%。2年與10年期利差收窄5.4個基點至24.5個基點，殖利率曲線呈牛市趨平。

隨著通過荷莫茲海峽的油輪增加、海灣供給恢復，布蘭特原油下跌4.33%至$73.74，WTI下跌3.92%至$70.34。汽油與餾分油庫存上升、煉油產能利用率偏高，加上出口復甦，市場因此淡化商用原油庫存減少610萬桶的影響。新屋銷售及建築許可疲弱，也從國內成長面增加持有債券的理由。與前一交易日不同，10年期殖利率的兩項組成因素均有貢獻：實質殖利率下降7.8個基點至2.201%，損益兩平通膨率下降2.7個基點至2.192%。

這波漲勢並未消除聯準會的緊縮傾向：市場仍反映約40個基點的額外緊縮，美元也走強。$700億5年期公債以4.200%的最高得標殖利率及2.35倍投標倍數順利標售，未使曲線中段漲勢反轉。信用市場仍具選擇性；投資級債受惠於政府債殖利率下降，高收益債近乎持平，而Hertz與Shapoorji Pallonji的動向凸顯個別發行人的再融資風險仍在。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied across the curve on June 24 as a further collapse in oil prices reduced the prospective inflation impulse and weak housing indicators added evidence that high borrowing costs are restraining an interest-sensitive part of the economy. The move was concentrated beyond the front end: the 5-year yield fell 9.2 basis points to 4.177%, the 10-year declined 10.5 basis points to 4.393% and the 30-year dropped 10.6 basis points to 4.841%, while the 2-year fell 5.1 basis points to 4.148%.

That distribution produced a bull flattening. The 2s10s curve narrowed 5.4 basis points to 24.5 basis points and 2s30s flattened 5.5 basis points to 69.3 basis points. Unlike the preceding session, when lower inflation compensation did most of the work, Wednesday’s nominal rally drew support from both components of the 10-year yield. The 10-year real yield fell 7.8 basis points to 2.201%, while the breakeven rate declined 2.7 basis points to 2.192%. Investors were marking down the energy risk embedded in inflation compensation and accepting a lower real return as weaker housing data and falling crude broadened demand for duration.

Brent settled 4.33% lower at $73.74 and WTI lost 3.92% to $70.34 as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased and physical supplies returned to markets disrupted by the U.S.-Iran conflict. The decline came despite a 6.1 million-barrel draw in U.S. commercial crude inventories. Rising gasoline and distillate stocks, refinery utilization of 96.1% and evidence that exports from the Gulf were recovering made the inventory headline less important than the wider improvement in product availability and shipping confidence.

The rally did not amount to a rejection of the Federal Reserve’s tightening bias. Markets still priced about 40 basis points of additional tightening after briefly discounting two full increases by mid-2027, and the dollar index rose 0.20% to 101.61. Gold futures fell 3.38% to $3,990.30, extending a retreat associated with higher U.S. rate expectations, dollar strength and reduced demand for geopolitical protection. The simultaneous rise in Treasuries and the dollar was consistent with a reassessment of how soon the Fed may need to act, not confidence that underlying inflation has already returned to target.

A $70 billion 5-year Treasury auction was absorbed at a 4.200% high yield with a 2.35 bid-to-cover ratio, allowing the belly rally to continue through a large supply event. Credit was more discriminating. Investment-grade bond prices benefited from the decline in government yields, but high-yield funds were nearly unchanged, while Hertz proposed an unusually defensive convertible financing and India’s Shapoorji Pallonji Group sought more time from creditors. The day therefore combined a broad rates rally with continued evidence that lower benchmark yields do not remove issuer-specific refinancing risk.

## Oil Relief Broadens the Treasury Rally

The most important change in the energy outlook was physical rather than diplomatic. Ships were moving through the Strait of Hormuz with their satellite signals switched on, indicating greater confidence among owners about safe passage. The International Maritime Organization said vessels could use Iranian waters or routes coordinated by Oman and the U.S. and that it had received safety guarantees covering hundreds of ships seeking to leave the Persian Gulf.

Fertilizer traffic also improved, with at least 16 vessels carrying crop nutrients exiting the strait and volumes moving closer to prewar levels. The United Arab Emirates had restored oil exports to almost 85% of their prewar pace in early June, according to the International Energy Agency, while Qatar expected to return liquefied-natural-gas output from undamaged facilities to normal levels within weeks. Those developments expanded the prospective supply response beyond Iranian barrels and reduced the probability that disrupted transit would sustain the earlier energy shock.

The political agreement remains incomplete. Washington and Tehran have offered conflicting accounts of nuclear inspections and control over released Iranian funds, and no arrangement has been reached for the long-term administration of the strait. Iran has sought a formal role and proposed insurance requirements that could generate fees, while continued fighting involving Israel and Iran-backed groups remains a possible route back to escalation. Markets nevertheless treated those risks as less immediate than the growing number of visible cargoes and the accumulation of oil offers in Europe and Asia.

That shift pushed WTI below $70 during the session before its $70.34 close, while Brent settled below $74. The daily losses took WTI’s 1-month decline to 27.18% and Brent’s to 28.78%. Falling spot and futures prices reduced the expected contribution of energy to headline inflation even though both central bankers and traders remained alert to the price increases already transmitted through production, transport and services.

The U.S. petroleum report showed why the inflation effect is not captured by crude stocks alone. Commercial crude inventories fell 6.1 million barrels to 412.1 million, about 7% below their 5-year seasonal average. Gasoline stocks increased 2.1 million barrels to 216.3 million, still about 5% below their 5-year average, and distillate inventories rose 3.1 million barrels to 106.1 million, about 10% below average. Refineries operated at 96.1% of capacity.

Four-week total products supplied averaged 20.5 million barrels a day, 2.1% more than a year earlier, but gasoline demand over the same period was 3.0% below its year-earlier pace. The figures describe a market in which refiners are running hard and product inventories are rebuilding even as crude stocks fall. That combination supported the view that the immediate shortage risk was easing, despite low absolute inventories and unresolved geopolitical terms.

Housing supplied the domestic-growth counterpart to the energy move. May new-home sales disappointed and building permits were weaker than expected, reinforcing the effect of restrictive mortgage rates on residential demand and construction. The releases did not by themselves establish a broader contraction, but they made it harder to treat the economy as uniformly resistant to high real rates. That mattered particularly for the 5- to 30-year sectors, where the market was balancing persistent inflation against the cumulative effect of restrictive financing conditions.

Treasury activity increased substantially as investors processed those signals. FINRA recorded $1.460 trillion of par trading, 29.0% more than on June 23, while nominal-coupon activity rose 29.9% to $1.111 trillion. Activity in maturities above 3 and through 5 years surged 61.4% to $335.0 billion, and turnover above 7 and through 10 years increased 41.9% to $196.2 billion. Those figures measure two-way transactions rather than net buying, but the concentration matched the sectors that led the rally and absorbed the day’s principal coupon auction.

TIPS trading rose a smaller 6.6% to $30.7 billion. The difference was consistent with the composition of the yield move: inflation compensation continued to decline, but the larger adjustment came through real yields. The 10-year real yield remained 5.5 basis points higher than a month earlier even after Wednesday’s fall, whereas the 10-year breakeven was 22.1 basis points lower. The session therefore reversed part of the post-Fed increase in real discount rates without restoring the inflation premium removed by the collapse in oil.

The dollar and precious metals preserved the other side of that policy repricing. The dollar index ended 1.52% higher over the week and 2.31% higher over the month. Gold fell below $4,000 an ounce for the first time since November and finished down 11.74% over the month. Silver fell more sharply, while weakness spread to platinum and palladium.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s emphasis on restoring price stability has strengthened the relative appeal of yield-bearing dollar assets, even though he stopped short of declaring rate increases the only available response. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he expected inflation to retreat as the Iran conflict subsided and expressed confidence that Warsh would balance inflation and growth independently. That expectation remains conditional: forecasts cited ahead of Thursday’s data put annual May PCE inflation at 4.1% and core inflation at 3.4%, still well above the Fed’s objective.

The S&P 500 slipped 0.10% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.43%, while the Dow gained 0.4%. The comparatively small index moves masked continued weakness in technology shares before Micron’s results and gains across a majority of S&P 500 constituents. Lower oil supported the broader market, but the prospect of restrictive rates continued to weigh on long-duration equity valuations. The VIX fell 4.41% to 18.63, showing that the session was not a generalized flight from risk even as Treasuries rallied.

## Five-Year Supply Clears as Leveraged Treasury Exposure Grows

Treasury’s new 5-year note stopped at 4.200% and carries a 4⅛% coupon. Investors submitted $164.427 billion of competitive bids for $69.855 billion accepted, producing a 2.35 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders received $43.028 billion and direct bidders $17.820 billion, leaving primary dealers with $9.006 billion. The notes settle June 30 and mature June 30, 2031.

Without a supplied when-issued reference, the auction cannot be characterized as a tail or a through. Its more useful signal was that a large intermediate-maturity offering cleared during a rally without forcing a reversal. Direct and indirect awards together accounted for most of the competitive issue, while dealer holdings were limited to less than $10 billion. The result extended the willingness to absorb policy-sensitive and intermediate duration that had appeared in the previous day’s 2-year sale.

The day’s floating-rate supply found still higher coverage. Treasury’s $28 billion reopening of a 1-year 10-month floating-rate note stopped at a 0.079% high discount margin, with a 0.103% spread and an index determination rate of 3.695%. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.99. Indirect bidders accepted $18.650 billion and dealers $9.331 billion of the $27.981 billion competitive award; direct bidders received none. The issue settles June 26 and matures April 30, 2028.

At the bill end, a $69 billion 119-day sale stopped at a 3.770% high discount rate and a 3.871% investment rate. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.55, and 11.15% of bids at the high rate were allotted. Indirect bidders took $37.414 billion, dealers $28.495 billion and direct bidders $2.573 billion of the competitive award. The bill settles June 30 and matures October 27. Neither the bill nor the floating-rate result indicated obvious difficulty absorbing cash-oriented supply, although the absence of when-issued references prevents a judgment about their pricing relative to pre-auction trading.

A newly published Federal Reserve study placed the primary-market results beside a longer-running change in Treasury intermediation. Principal economist Phillip Monin estimated that the cash-futures basis trade accounted for $830 billion of hedge funds’ long Treasury positions as of September, about twice its early-2020 peak and 35% of their total long exposure. The strategy pairs short Treasury futures with repo-financed holdings of deliverable cash securities, seeking to capture small pricing differences through substantial leverage.

Between September 2023 and September 2025, hedge funds’ gross Treasury exposure doubled to $4 trillion, comprising $2.4 trillion of long positions and $1.6 trillion of shorts. Basis and swap-spread arbitrage represented nearly half of the long positions, with the remainder distributed across yield-curve strategies, unencumbered cash holdings and long-only uses. Since the beginning of 2023, gross exposure, repo borrowing and monthly Treasury turnover had all more than doubled.

The concentration of those positions has also risen. The 50 largest funds accounted for 90% of total hedge-fund Treasury exposure, up from 84%. Monin said the scale, leverage and concentration could create systemic stress if several strategies came under pressure together or a severe shock affected the largest participants. The basis trade contributes to price discovery and liquidity in ordinary conditions, but the rapid unwinding of similar positions intensified Treasury-market turmoil in March 2020.

The findings describe the market’s structure rather than Wednesday’s investor direction. They nevertheless matter when daily cash activity is high and primary supply is large. Leveraged arbitrage can help connect auctioned securities with futures and repo markets, increasing capacity in normal trading. The same structure can transmit funding or volatility shocks rapidly if margins rise, repo terms tighten or relative-value relationships move against crowded positions.

## Credit Markets Separate Rate Relief From Refinancing Risk

The fall in Treasury yields lifted the LQD investment-grade bond fund by 0.46%, while high-yield prices were effectively flat: HYG slipped 0.03% and JNK declined 0.06%. The EMB emerging-market debt fund gained 0.32%. The pattern showed that duration benefited from the rates rally, but investors did not extend the same enthusiasm indiscriminately to lower-quality corporate risk.

The New York Fed’s June Corporate Bond Market Distress Index provided a broader measure of functioning. Market-level conditions improved during the month and ended slightly above the index’s historical 20th percentile. Investment-grade functioning was around its historical 50th percentile, while high-yield distress remained at historically low levels. The research measure combines primary issuance and pricing with secondary-market liquidity and trading indicators; it is distinct from the level or daily direction of credit spreads.

Those orderly aggregate conditions coexisted with acute issuer-specific pressure. Hertz announced a $300 million offering of convertible payment-in-kind notes alongside $100 million of newly issued shares intended to be borrowed and sold short by convertible investors. The structure addresses the scarcity of stock available to borrow because Hertz’s ownership is concentrated and its shares were already heavily shorted.

Payment in kind allows the company to avoid a conventional cash coupon, while the convertible structure should cost less than issuing straight high-yield debt. Hertz plans to use the proceeds to repay existing obligations, and part of its revolving credit facility expires this month, creating room for additional first-lien borrowing. The financing benefit comes with dilution: at the indicated price, the stock offering would exceed 25 million shares, equivalent to about 21% of the float.

The capital raise followed a warning that unexpected softness in used-car prices would increase depreciation expense. Hertz said adjusted corporate earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization would be no more than $80 million in the second quarter, below analysts’ expectations. Its shares fell 41%, their largest decline since the company’s 2021 listing. Lower Treasury yields reduced the benchmark component of financing costs, but the proposed terms reflected company-specific cash preservation and hedging constraints.

Shapoorji Pallonji Group confronted a more direct maturity problem. The Indian conglomerate offered bondholders a 30-basis-point fee to approve another extension of zero-coupon debt issued by Goswami Infratech. It is seeking to postpone repayment of 143 billion rupees, or about $1.5 billion, for at least a month beyond the June 30 maturity date.

The outstanding principal of the Goswami bonds has declined to 83.42 billion rupees since the securities were issued in 2023, but their yield has risen to 21.75% from 18.75% at issuance. The group is also seeking to extend a debt condition at financing unit Porteast Investment to September 30 from July 15. Porteast had temporarily increased the loan-to-value limit on a $3.4 billion loan to 40% from 34%, and the value of collateral backing the debt has fallen as Tata Consultancy Services shares traded near a 6-year low.

Most lenders have approved the proposed changes, but Ares Management was among those still negotiating. The debts are backed by the group’s 18.4% stake in Tata Sons. The request therefore remains a consent process, not a completed refinancing, and continued delay would preserve uncertainty over the eventual repayment of both Goswami and Porteast obligations.

Private-credit exposure supplied a different kind of warning. Hedge-fund manager Lee Robinson is using credit-default swaps to short insurers including Lincoln National, MetLife and Berkshire Hathaway, arguing that markets have not fully priced potential writedowns from private debt. Net notional positions in U.S. insurer CDS rose to $5.5 billion by May 22 from less than $4.9 billion at the end of 2025, while trading volumes and the cost of protection increased.

The thesis is not that large insurers face an immediate existential threat. MetLife has said about 95% of its private-debt portfolio is investment grade, well diversified and designed to perform through market cycles. A Moody’s analysis nevertheless found that illiquid assets, mostly private credit, represented one-fifth of U.S. life insurers’ $4 trillion of fixed-income holdings at the end of 2025, up from 18% a year earlier. Moody’s identified emerging stress in middle-market direct lending, including weaker credit quality and rising borrower pressure.

The contrast with the New York Fed distress index is material. Public corporate-bond markets continue to function smoothly and high-yield distress remains historically low, yet investors are paying more to hedge selected insurers against risks linked to less transparent private assets. Tight aggregate conditions can therefore coexist with a buildup of protection against a localized loss or liquidity event.

The search for additional yield is also changing the portfolios of corporate treasurers. A Clearwater Analytics study covering more than 400 companies with about $1 trillion of assets found that the median treasurer now holds 2% of its portfolio in Rule 144A bonds, compared with almost nothing several years ago. Such securities generally trade among qualified institutional buyers and can be less liquid than publicly registered bonds.

The private placements typically mature in 2 years or more and offer an average yield premium of about 52 basis points over comparable high-grade debt of similar duration. That extra income is drawing cash managers away from their traditional concentration in Treasury bills and commercial paper. Clearwater argued that systemic concerns are overstated but acknowledged idiosyncratic weaknesses, a distinction consistent with the orderly public-market distress readings and the more difficult financing faced by individual borrowers.

Argentina offered a sovereign example of improved funding conditions without a conventional international issue. The government assembled the dollars needed for a $4.2 billion bond payment due July 9 at an average hard-currency cost of about 6.7%, roughly 200 basis points below the estimated cost of issuing internationally. Treasury dollar deposits had reached about $3.6 billion, enough to cover approximately 85% of the payment, with the balance expected from local dollar placements, central-bank purchases and multilateral-backed financing.

The strategy benefited from ratings upgrades and a decline in country risk into the 430-basis-point area, at least 100 basis points lower than several months earlier. Argentina’s New York-law curve still yielded around 9%, leaving international borrowing expensive even after the improvement. The government has authorized as much as $5 billion of financing supported by institutions such as the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank, with Economy Minister Luis Caputo estimating a cost near 6%.

Avoiding Wall Street reduced the cost of meeting the immediate maturity, but it did not settle the refinancing plan for 2027. Analysts said Argentina could eventually issue $5 billion to $8 billion if external conditions remain supportive. The current achievement is narrower: the July payment has largely been funded without accepting the premium that global bond investors were demanding.

## Central Banks Retain Tightening Options Despite Cheaper Energy

The global policy response to falling oil was not uniform. In Japan, the Bank of Japan’s Summary of Opinions reinforced the case for additional increases after the policy rate was lifted to 1%, its highest since 1995. One board member said underlying inflation was approaching 2% and financial conditions remained accommodative, making continued increases appropriate as the economy and prices evolve.

Another opinion put the neutral rate around 2% and suggested considering increases at intervals of a few months. A separate member argued for moving closer to neutral as soon as possible. The BOJ’s own estimated neutral range is 1.1% to 2.5%, leaving the current rate near its lower boundary even after the June increase.

Governor Kazuo Ueda, in remarks delivered by Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino after Ueda’s return from hospital, said inflation could exceed the 2% target and reiterated that the bank would adjust accommodation in response to activity, prices and financial conditions. He made the timing and pace conditional partly on the Iran conflict. Business-service prices rose 3.3% from a year earlier for a third consecutive month, supporting concern that inflation pressure is not confined to imported goods.

The yen remained near 161.60 per dollar, close to its weakest level since 1986. That weakness raises imported inflation for a resource-dependent economy and leaves authorities alert to excessive currency moves. Political constraints remain: board member Toichiro Asada opposed the June increase, and another government appointee joins the board at month-end. The current communication nevertheless shows that a majority continues to view 1% as an accommodative setting rather than the endpoint.

India moved in the opposite market direction after Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said it was premature to discuss raising rates. He argued that officials would have shifted their stance from neutral to restrictive at the June meeting if tightening were sufficiently likely. The RBI instead held the policy rate at 5.25% and retained a data-dependent position.

India’s 10-year government yield fell 5 basis points to 6.82%, its lowest in 3 months, and 5-year overnight-indexed swaps dropped 10 basis points to 6.17%. Citigroup abandoned its call for increases during the current fiscal year, while HDFC Bank no longer expected a hike through fiscal 2027 unless weather-related inflation becomes persistent.

The qualifications remain significant. India imports about 90% of its oil, so the reversal in crude directly reduces its inflation exposure. But cumulative monsoon rainfall was 43% below normal as of June 22, threatening agricultural production and rural demand if the shortfall persists. Malhotra said food buffers were sufficient to mitigate weaker output, while emphasizing that the truce was fragile and oil supplies had not fully normalized.

China’s easing outlook also became less certain. Slightly more than half of 33 economists surveyed expected the People’s Bank of China to keep policy rates unchanged through 2026, while the remainder anticipated a small reduction by year-end. PBOC monetary-policy committee member Huang Yiping said a cut remained possible but was not assured and called for more targeted support for technology and household welfare.

China’s second-quarter economy has slowed, with May retail sales contracting for the first time since the reopening from pandemic restrictions and fixed-asset investment weakening more than expected. Exports and imports have been supported by the global AI investment boom, while oil prices remain above year-earlier levels. Consumer inflation stalled in May even as factory prices rose at the fastest pace in almost 4 years. Narrow bank margins, weak borrowing demand and the property downturn reduce the effectiveness of a broad rate cut, leaving the late-July Politburo meeting as the next major policy window.

The European Central Bank continued to signal that cheaper oil has not ended the tightening discussion. Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said further increases would probably be needed to return inflation to 2% over the medium term. She made the extent and timing conditional on the conflict, the economy and inflation but warned that the ceasefire was not a reason to relax.

Schnabel emphasized that forward energy prices remained elevated even after the spot-market retreat. She said May inflation showed some spread from the initial energy shock, although there was not yet evidence of second-round effects. Her assessment was that current rates were not restrictive and that the euro-area economy had been more resilient than expected. Most investors and economists anticipated at least one additional 25-basis-point increase, which would take the deposit rate to 2.5%.

Croatian central-bank Governor Ante Zigman added a new voice to the more inflation-focused side of the Governing Council. In his first public comments since taking office, he said price stability was the ECB’s priority and that reopening Hormuz would help inflation. His support for acting early reflected the tension facing the ECB: falling oil improves the prospective headline path, but officials remain concerned that the earlier shock has already entered broader pricing.

Germany’s ifo Business Climate Index offered modest growth relief. The headline measure rose to 85.6 in June from 85.0 in May as current assessments improved and expectations became somewhat less pessimistic. Manufacturing expectations strengthened, though current conditions weakened and new orders fell again. Sentiment improved in trade and construction, while services firms reported better current business but little change in expectations. The release reduced immediate downside concern without establishing a vigorous recovery.

Mexico produced a clearer inflation surprise ahead of its policy decision. Consumer prices in the first half of June were 3.55% higher than a year earlier, below every estimate in a survey whose median was 3.72%. Core inflation eased to 4.12%, approximately matching the 4.13% expectation. Weak domestic demand has helped contain prices, but services inflation is declining only gradually and food and energy remain volatile.

Banxico is expected to leave its overnight rate at 6.50%. Governor Victoria Rodríguez has said the current setting is appropriate to guide inflation toward the 3% target, while leaving open the possibility of another adjustment if weak demand persists and expectations remain anchored. The softer headline reading strengthens the dovish argument, but core inflation above 4% supports maintaining the post-cut pause while policymakers assess the durability of the improvement.

Singapore’s May core inflation held at 1.4%, below the 1.6% median estimate and unchanged from April, despite the global energy shock. The result supports expectations that the Monetary Authority of Singapore will leave its exchange-rate settings unchanged at its July decision after tightening in April. In Chile, meanwhile, minutes showed that all five central-bank board members regarded holding the policy rate at 4.5% as the only plausible June option. The U.S.-Iran accord reduced the probability of tighter policy, but officials wanted evidence that the peace process would endure before changing course.

Australia remained more firmly focused on domestic inflation. Reserve Bank Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the economy may be operating on a steeper part of the Phillips curve, where excess demand produces a larger inflation response. That was part of the rationale for increases at the first three meetings of the year. The bank paused at 4.35% last week but left another rise available.

Hauser argued that the same steepness could allow timely tightening to lower inflation with a smaller increase in unemployment. The RBA expects inflation to return to the midpoint of its 2%-3% target only in mid-2028, with unemployment peaking at 4.7%. Lower oil helps reduce the supply shock, but the bank’s concern remains that domestic inflation is too high and that full resolution of the Middle East conflict is not assured.

## Forward Market Significance

The immediate test is the U.S. data block at 08:30 ET on June 25: May PCE inflation, personal income and spending, durable-goods orders, the third estimate of Q1 GDP and initial jobless claims. Forecasts cited ahead of the release put annual headline PCE inflation at 4.1% and core inflation at 3.4%. Those readings would leave price growth well above target even after the collapse in oil.

The composition will matter as much as the inflation headline. Firm underlying prices and resilient spending would support the Fed’s tightening bias and test a Treasury rally that brought the 10-year real yield down almost 8 basis points. Softer demand or labor readings would reinforce the evidence from housing and increase the case for waiting, especially if core price pressure also moderates. The release will determine whether the day’s bull flattening represents a broader reassessment of restrictive policy or mainly relief from energy risk.

Treasury supply continues with $70 billion of 4-week bills and $75 billion of 8-week bills at 11:30 ET, followed by $44 billion of new 7-year notes at 13:00. All three auctions settle June 30. A nominal-coupon buyback covering securities with 20 to 30 years remaining runs from 13:40 to 14:00. The 7-year sale will test whether the demand that absorbed Wednesday’s 5-year note extends farther along the curve after 10- and 30-year yields fell more than 10 basis points.

The ECB publishes its Economic Bulletin at 10:00 CEST. Its detail on the June decision and staff projections will be assessed against Schnabel’s call for further increases, Zigman’s emphasis on price stability and the improvement in Germany’s ifo survey. The question is whether falling spot energy prices materially reduce medium-term inflation pressure or merely soften the near-term path after pass-through has already broadened.

Banco de México announces its decision at 15:00 ET, with the overnight rate at 6.50%. The lower-than-expected first-half June inflation reading gives policymakers more room to discuss eventual easing, but core inflation of 4.12% and persistent services pressure argue for caution. Guidance on weak domestic demand and the peso will be more consequential than an unchanged decision alone.

Preliminary June Tokyo CPI follows at 08:30 JST on June 26, providing the first current-month inflation test after the BOJ raised its rate to 1%. A firm result, particularly in underlying components, would support the board members calling for increases at intervals of a few months. A softer reading would give greater weight to Ueda’s conditional language and the political resistance to a rapid normalization path.

The final University of Michigan survey and the New York Fed’s Multivariate Core Trend Inflation measure arrive at 10:00 ET on June 26. Michigan’s preliminary reading put sentiment at 48.9, 1-year inflation expectations at 4.6% and long-run expectations at 3.4%. Revisions will show whether the retreat in oil has begun to change household views, while the New York Fed measure will provide a separate check on whether underlying inflation remains consistent with the Fed’s more restrictive stance.

section_summaries.summary: The Treasury rally broadened from lower inflation compensation into a decline in real yields as cheaper oil and weak housing increased demand for duration. Intermediate and long yields fell more than the 2-year yield, producing a bull flattening, while the 5-year auction cleared smoothly. Continued Fed tightening expectations and difficult issuer financings showed that lower energy and benchmark yields had not removed inflation or credit risk.

section_summaries.next_check: Whether safer Gulf transit and restored exports persist despite incomplete political arrangements.
section_summaries.section_title: Oil Relief Broadens the Treasury Rally
section_summaries.summary: Visible tanker and fertilizer traffic through Hormuz, recovering Gulf exports and Qatar's expected LNG normalization reduced the immediate supply threat despite unresolved political terms. Product inventories rebuilt as refineries ran at 96.1%, making the crude-stock draw less decisive. Weak housing data reinforced the duration bid, while elevated policy expectations, a firmer dollar and falling precious metals showed that cheaper oil had not settled the inflation outlook.

section_summaries.market_read: Leveraged relative-value trades can support liquidity in normal markets but transmit stress rapidly when margins or repo terms tighten.
section_summaries.section_title: Five-Year Supply Clears as Leveraged Treasury Exposure Grows
section_summaries.summary: The $70 billion 5-year note cleared at 4.200% with a 2.35 bid-to-cover ratio, and direct and indirect bidders took most of the competitive issue without disrupting the rally. Separate Federal Reserve research estimated the cash-futures basis trade at $830 billion and showed hedge-fund Treasury exposure becoming larger, more leveraged and more concentrated, expanding normal intermediation capacity but increasing vulnerability to funding or volatility shocks.

section_summaries.market_read: Benchmark-rate relief lowered the government-yield component of financing costs without resolving borrower-specific constraints.
section_summaries.next_check: Whether Shapoorji Pallonji secures creditor consent before the June 30 maturity.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Markets Separate Rate Relief From Refinancing Risk
section_summaries.summary: Lower Treasury yields supported investment-grade bonds, but high-yield prices were nearly unchanged as aggregate public credit markets remained orderly. Hertz's defensive convertible financing, Shapoorji Pallonji's extension requests and increased insurer hedging against private-credit exposure showed that benign market-wide conditions can coexist with acute refinancing, liquidity and asset-quality concerns. Argentina separately funded most of its July payment below the estimated cost of an international issue.

section_summaries.next_check: China's late-July Politburo meeting is the next major window for broader or more targeted support.
section_summaries.section_title: Central Banks Retain Tightening Options Despite Cheaper Energy
section_summaries.summary: Cheaper oil changed near-term inflation risks without producing a uniform policy response. BOJ and ECB officials retained a tightening bias, the RBI pushed back against imminent increases, and China's easing outlook became less certain. Softer inflation supported patience in Mexico and Singapore, while Australia remained focused on domestic price pressure. Currency weakness, food risks and earlier energy pass-through kept policy paths conditional.

The June 25 U.S. inflation and demand releases will test whether the bull flattening reflects a broader reassessment of restrictive policy or mainly relief from energy risk. The new 7-year note will test demand farther along the curve after the 5-year sale cleared smoothly. The ECB Bulletin and subsequent inflation releases will show whether policymakers treat cheaper spot energy as a medium-term shift or only a softer near-term path.

overall_summary.headline: Oil slide and weak housing drive a bull-flattening Treasury rally
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied across the curve, led by intermediate and long maturities. The 5-year yield fell 9.2 basis points to 4.177%, the 10-year declined 10.5 basis points to 4.393% and the 30-year dropped 10.6 basis points to 4.841%, while the 2-year fell 5.1 basis points to 4.148%. The move bull-flattened 2s10s by 5.4 basis points to 24.5 basis points.

Brent fell 4.33% to $73.74 and WTI lost 3.92% to $70.34 as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased and Gulf supplies returned. Rising gasoline and distillate stocks, high refinery utilization and recovering exports outweighed a 6.1 million-barrel crude draw. Weak new-home sales and building permits added a domestic-growth reason to own duration. Unlike the preceding session, both components of the 10-year yield contributed: the real yield fell 7.8 basis points to 2.201% and the breakeven declined 2.7 basis points to 2.192%.

The rally did not erase the Fed's tightening bias: markets still priced about 40 basis points of additional tightening, and the dollar strengthened. A $70 billion 5-year auction cleared at 4.200% with a 2.35 bid-to-cover ratio without reversing the belly rally. Credit remained selective, as investment-grade bonds benefited from lower government yields while high yield was nearly unchanged and Hertz and Shapoorji Pallonji highlighted continuing issuer-specific refinancing risk.
overall_summary.summary: Treasury yields fell most beyond the front end as recovering Gulf shipments reduced the prospective energy-inflation impulse and weak housing data reinforced the drag from restrictive borrowing costs, although continued Fed tightening expectations and issuer-specific refinancing strains limited the broader relief.
